I will keep my land mostly in the wheat-maize rotation, because that is the steadiest way for me to protect grain output and cash flow in Quzhou County. The land, water, and machinery around me all fit that system, and I know how to manage it without taking too much market risk. I will put most of my fields into winter wheat first and then summer maize right after harvest, because that gives me two crops from the same land in one year and makes full use of the season. I will keep a small piece in spring peanuts, not to chase something fancy, but to spread risk a little, improve the rotation on that plot, and leave myself one crop that needs less irrigation than maize. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it clearly helps stand, yield, and uniformity, but I will not overpush fertilizer or sprays because my margin depends on controlling cost as much as yield. On wheat I will focus on good basal fertilizer, one topdressing at jointing, timely watering at key stages, and disease control if rust or aphids show up. On maize I will sow quickly after wheat harvest, keep plant density even, push nitrogen more on the main grain field, and irrigate at the critical stages if water is available. On peanuts I will keep fertilizer moderate, avoid too much nitrogen, and manage weeds and leaf disease early. I will use rotary tillage on most fields because it is practical for me, fast, and matches the equipment I can get.
